in_arabic.name: ذَكَاوَان
in_arabic.meaning: منظور عظيم، ذاكر للخير، ذو نظر واسع
in_arabic.long_meaning: ذَكَاوَان: اسم من أصل عربي، مشتق من الجذر ذَكَاة، يُفيد النظر، الذاكرة، الفهم. يُستخدم في الاسم لتشجيع الأطفال على النظر إلى الأمور من منظور عظيم، والذاكرة للخير، والفهم الواسع للعوالم. في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية، يُعتبر إسم ذَكَاوَان اسمًا للناس الذين يتمتعون بالذكاء، والفصاحة، والذاكرة العالية. من أصل عربي، ويتسم بالجمال والاستقامة في التركيب اللغوي.

in_urdu.name: ذَكاوان
in_urdu.meaning: بڑے منظر کا مالک، خیروں کا ذاکر، وسیع نظر رکھنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: ذَكاوان: اردو زبان میں ایک اسلامی نام ہے جو عرب زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اس نام کے متعلقہ معنی ہیں کہ ایک بڑے منظر کا مالک ہو، خیروں کا ذاکر ہو، وسیع نکتہ نظر رکھنے والا ہو۔ اس نام سے ایسے والدین اپنے بیٹوں کو نام دیتے ہیں جو ان کے لیے بہت اہمیت کا حامل ہوتا ہے۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کی ثقافت میں خاص مقام رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: धकावान
in_hindi.meaning: बड़े दृष्टिकोण वाला, अच्छाइयों का याददाश्त रखने वाला, विस्तृत दृष्टिकोण वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: धकावान: हिंदी भाषा में एक इस्लामी नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसके अर्थ हैं कि वह व्यक्ति अपने बड़े दृष्टिकोण के साथ अच्छाइयों का याददाश्त रखता है और विस्तृत दृष्टिकोण से देखता है। इस नाम को भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत महत्व दिया जाता है। यह नाम उन माता-पिता द्वारा अपने बच्चों को दिया जाता है जो उनके लिए महत्वपूर्ण होता है।

in_pashto.name: ذکاوان
in_pashto.meaning: نظرونه سترګه، ګټوروګانې یادښتولونکی، ښکلې پکتونکې

in_english.name: Dhakawaan
in_english.meaning: One with great vision, remembers goodness, has a wide perspective
in_english.long_meaning: Dhakawaan: A name of Arabic origin, derived from the root ذَكَاة, meaning to see, remember, and understand. It is a name that encourages children to have a great vision, remember goodness, and have a wide perspective. In some Islamic cultures, it is considered a name for people who possess intelligence, eloquence, and high memory. Of Arabic origin, it is characterized by its beauty and stability in linguistic structure.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dhakawaan" holds a significant cultural impact within the Islamic community, as it represents a person who exhibits strength and courage in their faith and actions. This can be seen through various aspects of Islamic culture, such as the martial arts tradition of "Dhikr" (remembrance of Allah), where individuals engage in physical training and mental focus to purify their souls and strengthen their connection with Allah. Additionally, the name can be associated with military prowess and the defense of Islamic lands and values, as seen in historical figures like Saladin and Umar ibn Al-Khattab who were renowned for their battlefield victories and commitment to the faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Dhakawaan" lies in its emphasis on jihad, which is often translated as struggle or striving in the way of Allah. It is a reminder that every believer is called upon to engage in this personal and collective struggle towards self-improvement, the betterment of the community, and the establishment of the divine rule on earth. By embracing the identity of a "Dhakawaan," one is not only acknowledging the desire and capacity to physically defend the faith but also accepting the responsibility to spiritually and morally uplift oneself and others through acts of kindness, wisdom, patience, and piety. This call to jihad echoes directly from the Quran and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), who taught that striving in the way of Allah is an obligation for all sincere and committed believers. Therefore, "Dhakawaan" is a name that carries deep spiritual significance as it underscores the essential aspects of personal growth, communal well-being, and devotion to Allah.
